auditor.opinionText: The consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of the Group as at December 31, 2024, in accordance with IFRS as endorsed in the Kingdom and SOCPA pronouncements.
auditor.materiality: SAR 30.0 billion overall Group materiality (2023: SAR 30.0 billion); misstatements above SAR 2.3 billion reported to governance

kams.title: Recoverability of goodwill and brand recognised on the SABIC acquisition
kams.summary: Goodwill of SAR 99.1 billion and the indefinite-life brand of SAR 18.1 billion are tested annually using 10-year discounted cash-flow value-in-use models. No impairment was identified.

kams.title: Recoverability of property, plant and equipment
kams.summary: Impairment indicators were identified for certain Downstream cash-generating units; an aggregate impairment charge of SAR 10.4 billion was recorded based on value-in-use models.

brief:
Saudi Aramco closed FY2024 with revenue of SAR 1,637,299 million, down 1.0% on 2023, while net income fell 12.4% to SAR 398,422 million as other income related to sales [[n:24]] declined and purchases [[n:25]] rose. The Downstream segment swung to a loss before interest and tax of SAR 10,998 million [[n:4]], partly reflecting a SAR 10,370 million impairment of plant and equipment [[n:5]].

The balance sheet remains very strong: total equity of SAR 1,651,355 million against total borrowings of SAR 319,290 million [[n:20]]. However, dividends of SAR 465,918 million [[n:36]] exceeded operating cash flow net of capex, and short-term investments were drawn down from SAR 184,343 million to SAR 13,186 million [[n:14]], moving the Group from a net cash position of SAR 102,753 million to net debt of SAR 78,078 million (gearing 4.5%) [[n:3]].

The auditor's opinion is unmodified. Reviewers should focus on the SABIC goodwill test (SAR 99,116 million, 11.0% discount rate) [[n:6]], guarantees to Sadara and Petro Rabigh [[n:33]], SAR 223,301 million of contracted capital commitments [[n:32]], and the Government's role as 81.48% shareholder, tax authority and largest customer [[n:1]] [[n:29]].

lens.headline: Government retains 81.48% after the June 2024 secondary offering; PIF and Sanabil hold a further 16%.
lens.detail: Share capital of SAR 90,000 million is divided into 242 billion shares. The Government sold ~1.7 billion shares (0.7%) in June 2024, and 137.6 million were bought back as treasury shares for SAR 3,750 million for employee share plans. The Group consolidates 100+ subsidiaries and holds 70% of SABIC.

lens.headline: The Government is shareholder, regulator, tax authority and the largest related party: SAR 745,931 million was paid in taxes, royalties and dividends in 2024.
lens.detail: Payments to the Government comprised income taxes SAR 176,523 million, royalties SAR 187,982 million and dividends SAR 381,426 million. Other income related to sales (SAR 164,375 million) compensates the Company for Kingdom-regulated prices; SAR 38,274 million was due from the Government at year-end. Transactions with Government entities are on 'specific terms within the relevant regulatory framework'.

lens.headline: Gearing moved from net cash (6.3)% to 4.5% net debt as cash and short-term investments funded dividends; SAR 37,500 million of revolving facilities remain undrawn.
lens.detail: Total borrowings SAR 319,290 million (debentures SAR 106,283 million; sukuk SAR 41,389 million; leases SAR 62,483 million). Finance costs rose to SAR 10,540 million with a further SAR 8,692 million capitalised. Covenants limit liens and asset disposals; interest-rate sensitivity is SAR 605 million per 1 percentage point.

lens.headline: SAR 223,301 million of capital expenditure is contracted but not yet incurred, plus SAR 38,496 million of leases not yet commenced.
lens.detail: Cash capex reached SAR 188,890 million (Upstream SAR 147,135 million). Additional commitments include 18 offshore rigs for IMI (SAR 20,250 million), 40 onshore rigs for ARM (SAR 7,667 million), capital contributions to affiliates of SAR 3,865 million and solar project equity bridge loans guaranteed via SAPCO.

lens.headline: Guarantees extend to Sadara senior debt (up to SAR 13,875 million with Dow), Petro Rabigh debt service undertakings, equity bridge loans and SAR 1,855 million of other affiliate borrowings.
lens.detail: Sadara's SAR 37,280 million project debt was restructured with a grace period to June 2026 and maturity 2038; Petro Rabigh's revolving facilities were fully drawn (SAR 5,625 million) and a phased waiver agreed in August 2024. The Company will raise its Petro Rabigh stake to 60% in 2025 for SAR 2,632 million.

lens.headline: PP&E impairment of SAR 10,370 million (2023: SAR 3,110 million) on Downstream facilities; SABIC goodwill (SAR 99,116 million) and brand (SAR 18,140 million) passed impairment tests.
lens.detail: Impairments were driven by revised cash-flow projections at pre-tax discount rates of 8.3%–11.6%. The goodwill test used an 11.0% pre-tax discount rate and 2.25% terminal growth; a rate of 11.8% would eliminate headroom. Both items were key audit matters.

lens.headline: Upstream earned SAR 801,047 million before interest and tax; Downstream recorded a loss of SAR 10,998 million. 58% of external revenue is In-Kingdom.
lens.detail: External revenue: Upstream SAR 719,157 million, Downstream SAR 917,044 million. Out-of-Kingdom revenue of SAR 683,160 million includes SAR 190,011 million originating from the USA. In-Kingdom long-lived assets total SAR 1,500,218 million.

lens.headline: Effective rate 49.1%; the 20% Downstream tax rate is conditional on separating Downstream activities, with an extension to December 31, 2030 'in progress'.
lens.detail: Income tax and zakat expense was SAR 383,588 million. If the separation condition were not met, Downstream activities would be retroactively taxed at 50%. Tax filings up to 2019 are accepted; unrecognised deferred tax assets on unused losses amount to SAR 17,113 million. No material Pillar Two exposure.

lens.headline: Carrying value of joint ventures and associates is SAR 65,261 million; the Group acquired Esmax (Chile) for SAR 1,373 million and is divesting Hadeed, Film & Sheet and ALBA.
lens.detail: Largest equity-accounted holdings: Yanpet SAR 9,320 million, Clariant SAR 5,690 million, Kemya SAR 5,575 million. Hadeed was sold to PIF in May 2024 (SAR 1,163 million cash plus deferred consideration); ALBA (SAR 3,294 million) was held for sale and sold in February 2025 for ~SAR 3,612 million.

lens.headline: Dividends paid of SAR 465,918 million (SAR 1.9260 per share) included SAR 161,593 million of performance-linked dividends; a further SAR 80,104 million was declared in March 2025.
lens.detail: Dividends exceeded net income of SAR 398,422 million, reducing unappropriated retained earnings from SAR 1,411,474 million to SAR 1,342,442 million. The March 2025 dividend cut the performance-linked component to SAR 822 million.

lens.headline: PwC issued an unmodified opinion on March 3, 2025 with two key audit matters; statements approved by the Board the same day.
lens.detail: Materiality was set at SAR 30.0 billion. Key management compensation was SAR 182 million. Subsequent events include the completion of the ALBA sale on February 19, 2025.

lens.headline: Employee benefit expense SAR 67,401 million; net post-employment benefit position is an asset of SAR 499 million.
lens.detail: Subsidised employee home loans total SAR 15,706 million. Share-based compensation of SAR 593 million relates to ESPP, ELTIP, MLTIP and LTIP plans using treasury shares. The new Social Insurance Law (July 2024) had no material impact.
